interpretive_essays.title: Infrastructure is not service
interpretive_essays.thesis: Physical assets and institutional programs become public value only through a chain of accepted, repeated service that must be observed rather than assumed.

sections.heading: The visible asset
sections.text: A fab expansion, a new manufacturing line, and a reservoir system are tangible. Their visibility makes them tempting proxies for delivery. The Phase 178 records preserve a harder distinction: an official funding or forecast record establishes a named intervention, not a universal operating state.

sections.heading: The missing receiver
sections.text: Service evidence requires a receiver and acceptance rule. Semiconductor output needs a qualified product, customer or program acceptance, period, and denominator. Water operations need delivered volumes by right class and period. Without that receiving side, capacity and benefit remain open questions.

sections.heading: The recurring test
sections.text: A single sample, ceremony, forecast, or delivery can be a real milestone and still fail to establish dependable operation. Recurrence, revisions, downtime, exclusions, and method continuity determine whether the record can support a service claim.

sections.heading: Editorial consequence
sections.text: The Atlas therefore publishes the asset, authority, and open bridge together. It refuses a synthetic place stage and asks for the next record that would connect the asset to accepted operation.

interpretive_essays.title: Selection is not capacity
interpretive_essays.thesis: A selection, proposal, or award is an institutional commitment state; capacity begins only when a defined system can produce accepted output under a stated period and denominator.

sections.heading: Commitment has stages
sections.text: Proposed funding, a signed direct award, obligation, expenditure, construction, commissioning, qualification, and recurring production are different states. Collapsing them turns program administration into a performance claim.

sections.heading: Amounts need denominators
sections.text: An up-to amount may cover several sites or workstreams. The Beaverton–Camas proposal shows why a shared ceiling cannot be duplicated across places; the Malta award shows why a portfolio amount cannot become one facility's capacity figure without allocation.

sections.heading: Capacity needs an operating definition
sections.text: Installed equipment, nameplate potential, qualified throughput, accepted output, and utilization answer different questions. A credible capacity statement must identify product, line, unit, period, method, exclusions, and receiving authority.

sections.heading: What the resource can say now
sections.text: These records map where public commitments are aimed and which supply-chain nodes they touch. They do not yet demonstrate how much dependable domestic output exists or what outcome the investment caused.

interpretive_essays.title: Demonstration is not operations
interpretive_essays.thesis: A demonstration shows that a bounded event occurred; operations require an authorized, accepted, repeatable service record with performance and failure boundaries.

sections.heading: Three different milestone types
sections.text: FAA's hybrid-electric flights are demonstrations, DSS-23 is described by NASA as beginning mission communications after testing, and Roseville reports sample production. Each is meaningful, but each sits at a different point in its own technical and institutional chain.

sections.heading: Authorization and acceptance
sections.text: A route demonstration does not supply aircraft certification or scheduled-service authority. An operating antenna milestone does not by itself quantify network-wide availability. Sample production does not establish a qualified commercial line. The relevant receiver and acceptance test differ in every system.

sections.heading: Repeatability and denominator
sections.text: Operations claims need a period, service unit, denominator, failure treatment, and revision policy. Flight count, supported communication passes, accepted wafer output, and uptime cannot be pooled merely because each is described as progress.

sections.heading: The useful bounded claim
sections.text: The resource can state the exact event, date, issuer, and excluded inference. That makes milestones informative without converting them into premature claims of commercial service, total capacity, reliability, or success.

interpretive_essays.title: Measurement without compatible denominators is not comparison
interpretive_essays.thesis: Comparison becomes evidence only when entity, period, measure, method, denominator, jurisdiction, and revision treatment are compatible—or when the noncomparability is itself made explicit.

sections.heading: Shared labels conceal different units
sections.text: Funding, capacity, output, service, adoption, and benefit are not interchangeable. Even two semiconductor facilities may produce different products on different tools for different receivers, while a basin forecast uses an entirely different population and time basis.

sections.heading: Geography is not a denominator
sections.text: Naming Beaverton, Camas, Malta, or Yakima locates a record but does not define what is counted. Site allocation, product boundary, right class, customer cohort, and observation period must be present before a rate or total can travel across records.

sections.heading: Noncomparability is a result
sections.text: A Context only verdict is not editorial failure. It prevents false rankings and identifies exactly which fields must be acquired before a comparison can be made.

sections.heading: A better next move
sections.text: Instead of forcing a common score, the overlays preserve each source's state and publish decisive next artifacts. Future comparison can then begin from compatible accepted records, not from narrative similarity.
